goals: PRIMARY (management scenario): quantify decadal water-level recovery from a 30% cut in agricultural groundwater pumping
SUPPORTING (mechanistic): estimate spatially-variable groundwater recharge under real soils/forcing as a boundary condition
VALIDATION: compare simulated water-table depth to USGS well observations
key_processes: lateral & regional groundwater flow and storage recovery

model_choice.rationale: ELM can only supply recharge (QDRAI) as a boundary flux; it cannot represent pumping, lateral flow, or regional water-table recovery, which are the mechanisms the question requires.
model_choice.coupling_note: Answering the recovery question needs ELM recharge -> a groundwater flow model (PFLOTRAN) with an explicit pumping/extraction boundary condition and lateral flow. That coupler and the pumping BC do not exist; PFLOTRAN here is also only steady-state, not the transient decadal solver required.

answerable: spatially-variable groundwater recharge (QDRAI) under real soils and NLDAS forcing, with spin-up
diagnostic comparison of 1-D equilibrium water-table depth to USGS wells (with warm start; drift expected)

not_answerable.why: ELM has no representation of anthropogenic groundwater extraction; there is no lever to impose or reduce pumping, and pumping records are missing from the brief
not_answerable.needs: groundwater pumping/extraction boundary condition + pumping records dataset

not_answerable.why: single-column ELM has no lateral transport and no regional water table; recovery is a lateral-flow/regional-storage process ELM cannot simulate
not_answerable.needs: ELM->PFLOTRAN coupling with lateral groundwater flow and a transient (not steady-state) solver

not_answerable.why: columns are independent 1-D points; no aggregation/routing to a connected aquifer
not_answerable.needs: coupled groundwater flow model driven by ELM recharge

sampling_strategy.n_justification: Only the recharge sub-product is feasible; recharge is dominated by soil texture (3 classes) with a secondary low/upland split (2 bands) = 6 groups. Larger N cannot help because the primary mechanism (pumping) is unrepresentable regardless of sampling density.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate in agricultural valley/lowland areas (the pumped zone of interest and where recharge-to-aquifer coupling matters most), with upland columns to span the recharge gradient.
sampling_strategy.replication: None — N is deliberately minimal because the design only produces a boundary-condition sub-product, not the requested answer.

sampling_plan.reason: high-recharge lowland agricultural soil; dominant recharge signal near the pumped aquifer.
typical lowland loam; baseline agricultural recharge in the extraction zone.
low-permeability lowland; low-recharge end member near wells.
spans elevation gradient of recharge on coarse substrate.
upland loam recharge; contrasts with valley loam.

validation_design.comparison: co-located (nearest well to column) — but DIAGNOSTIC ONLY: ELM's 1-D equilibrium differs from the real lateral-flow water table, and this comparison cannot attribute or test any pumping effect
validation_design.metric: bias + RMSE against warm-start equilibrium; report drift as a result
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on USGS well density in HUC 07060002

validation_design.comparison: no observations; recharge is delivered as a coupling boundary condition, sanity-checked against literature basin recharge rates only

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS forcing, native SSURGO soil, multi-year spin-up + WTD-informed warm start

requires_capabilities.why: the scenario is defined by a 30% pumping change, which no model in the stack can currently impose
brief lists pumping records as MISSING; baseline extraction is needed before any 30% reduction can be applied

requires_capabilities.capability: ELM->PFLOTRAN weak coupling (recharge -> transient groundwater BC)
requires_capabilities.why: recovery requires lateral flow and regional storage that single-column ELM lacks

requires_capabilities.capability: transient groundwater solver (PFLOTRAN is steady-state here)
regional water-table / lateral groundwater flow representation
requires_capabilities.why: recovery propagates laterally; independent 1-D columns cannot capture it
recharge and water-table states are init-sensitive; needed even for the recharge sub-product

assumptions: The 30% reduction and any pumping baseline would have to be supplied externally; none is in the brief.
SSURGO soil texture is available in-domain for stratification.
160 m relief and 12 km NLDAS mean elevation/forcing effects on recharge are minor; soil is the dominant control.
USGS well data can be co-located but only supports diagnostic ZWT comparison, not pumping attribution.
open_questions: Can pumping/withdrawal records (volumes, well locations, timing) be obtained for the basin?
Is there appetite to build the ELM->PFLOTRAN transient coupling with a pumping BC — the only path to answering the question?
What aquifer are the target USGS wells screened in, and is it the same unit being pumped agriculturally?
Would a purpose-built groundwater model (e.g. MODFLOW) with pumping wells be a better tool than this land-surface stack for this management question?
